How Claude Code Works

Understand the agentic loop, built-in tools, context management, and the different permission modes.

The Agentic Loop

Claude Code isn't a chatbot that replies and waits. It runs an agentic loop: receive a goal → plan → take actions → observe results → continue until done (or until it needs your input).

1
You give a goal
e.g. "fix the login bug"
2
Claude plans
Reads relevant files, understands context
3
Claude acts
Edits files, runs commands, calls tools
4
Claude observes
Reads output, checks tests, verifies
5
Repeat or stop
Continues until done or asks you

Built-in Tools

Claude has access to these tools during every session:

Read / Write / Edit
Read files, create new files, or edit existing ones with precise diffs
Bash
Run shell commands — tests, builds, git operations, any CLI tool
Glob / Grep
Find files by pattern or search content across your codebase
WebFetch
Fetch URLs for docs, API references, issue tracker content
TodoWrite
Maintain a task list for multi-step operations
AskUserQuestion
Pause and ask you something before proceeding (used in Plan Mode)

The Context Window — Your #1 Resource

The context window holds your entire conversation: every message, every file Claude read, every command output. Performance degrades as it fills.

▸
Track usage: Add a custom status line via /statusline
▸
Clear context: /clear — reset between unrelated tasks
▸
Compact manually: /compact — summarize to free space
▸
Targeted compact: Esc+Esc → select message → Summarize from here
▸
Use subagents: Delegate research so it doesn't fill YOUR context

Permission Modes

Press Shift+Tab to cycle through these modes during a session:

Normal Mode
default
Claude asks before modifying files or running commands. Safest.
Auto-Accept Mode
⏵⏵ accept edits on
Approves all file edits automatically. Still asks for Bash commands.
Plan Mode
⏸ plan mode on
Read-only. Claude can explore but not change anything. Perfect for research.
bash
"color:#586e75"># Start directly in Plan Mode
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --permission-mode plan

"color:#586e75"># Run a one-off headless query in Plan Mode
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude --permission-mode plan -p "analyze the auth system"

Plan Mode Workflow

For complex multi-file changes, use this 4-phase workflow:

E
ExplorePlan Mode
“read /src/auth and understand how sessions work”
P
PlanPlan Mode
“I want to add Google OAuth — create a detailed plan”
I
ImplementNormal Mode
“implement the OAuth flow from your plan, run tests”
C
CommitNormal Mode
“commit with a descriptive message and open a PR”
Press Ctrl+G in Plan Mode to open the plan in your editor before Claude proceeds with implementation.

Extended Thinking (ultrathink)

Extended thinking is on by default — Claude reasons through complex problems before responding. You can see this reasoning with Ctrl+O (verbose mode).

bash
"color:#586e75"># Include "ultrathink" in any prompt for maximum reasoning depth
"color:#586e75"># Works with Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6
"color:#7c3aed;font-weight:600">claude
> ultrathink: design the best database schema for our multi-tenant SaaS
Toggle thinking
Alt+T (Win/Linux) or Option+T (Mac)
Effort level
/model → set low/medium/high
Force deep think
add "ultrathink" to your prompt
View reasoning
Ctrl+O to toggle verbose mode

Checkpointing & Rewind

Every action Claude takes creates a checkpoint automatically. You can restore conversation, code, or both to any point — even across sessions.

bash
"color:#586e75"># Open the rewind menu
Esc Esc   (or /rewind)

"color:#586e75"># From the menu you can:
"color:#586e75"># • Restore code only
"color:#586e75"># • Restore conversation only  
"color:#586e75"># • Restore both
"color:#586e75"># • Summarize from a selected message
Checkpoints only track changes made by Claude, not external processes. This is not a replacement for git.
